overview: White fianchettoes with g3 and develops the knight to f3, hitting e5, and Black can answer with ...e4 to chase the knight (a reversed Alekhine-style tempo game) or just defend with ...Nc6. The line is a move-order idea more than a theoretical variation. Play is slow and strategic, usually transposing into King's Indian Attack, Réti or English positions.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto and long-diagonal pressure on e5/b7
Play d3 and e4 to complete a King's Indian Attack set-up
Meet ...e4 with Nd4 and aim at the e4 pawn

black_ideas.idea: Gain space with ...e4 and ...d5, using the loss of tempo by the knight
Develop ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and keep a central pawn pair
Fianchetto the bishop and stay compact

typical_structures.structure: Flank-opening structures with Black's centre pawns against a g2 bishop

character.notes: Slow, low-risk fianchetto play with few early tactics.

approach.notes: Part of the g3/Nf3 family; not a clear system on its own.

level.notes: Easy to play but transposes widely.

character.reason: Slow fianchetto set-up without forcing lines.

structure.reason: A flank opening with an undecided centre.

approach.reason: Close to a move order; transposes into KIA, Réti or English.

level.reason: Simple moves but the structures vary.

plans.reason: The g2 bishop on the long diagonal is the core idea.
